correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the common continuous null to a uniform fixed-composition binary word. Word reversal proves the odd cross-moment vanishes. For the squared centered Mann–Whitney statistic, conditioning on each adjacent transition reduces the calculation to exact simple-random-sampling inclusion moments; summing uses the explicit centered-rank square sum and the exact identity for the adjacent coefficient sums. The fourth centered moment follows independently from the two-letter Gaussian-binomial cumulant generating function. The exact checker exhaustively verifies all displayed finite formulas for every positive sample-size pair with pooled size at most 14. No finite computation is used to establish the universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The two statistics are classical distribution-free tests aimed at different departures from a common two-sample null. The exact zero first-order covariance can suggest orthogonality, but the new formula shows a strict negative coupling with the natural two-sided squared rank-sum evidence at every nontrivial finite sample size. The standardized covariance has a compact closed form and a nonzero proportional-sample limit, while the correlation has a universal first-order decay independent of the sample fraction. This identifies a concrete dependence structure relevant to combining or comparing the two tests and is not a mere reparameterization of known marginal moments.
